tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST
tiles.details: Find an erect warm-season perennial tuft with a narrow ~3–10 cm flowering raceme. The dark awns arise from fertile spikelets and can form an orderly spire before tangling at maturity. Panels 1 and 3 show flowering architecture and a genuine mature tangle, but neither alone proves the sessile/pedicelled pairing or a sharp basal callus.
tiles.short: One narrow raceme; long dark awns twist into a mature tangle
tiles.status: FIELD-READY HABIT; ATTACHED PAIR MACRO GAP

tiles.heading: 02 · CHECK THE TRUE LEAF COLLAR
tiles.details: At the inner blade–sheath junction, lift the blade to expose the short pale membrane and its fringed margin. Panels 4–5 are authentic Harry Rose collar close-ups; longer adjacent sheath-mouth hairs are separate and must not be measured as the ligule. Published treatments differ in describing a hair fringe versus a ciliate membrane; keep the distinction visible.
tiles.short: ~1 mm ciliate membranous ligule; separate sheath hairs

tiles.heading: 03 · FIND THE TWO SPIKELETS AT ONE NODE
tiles.details: Trace a single rachis joint under 10–20×. Basal pairs can be similar-looking and awnless; upper pairs differ: a fertile sessile unit with one long awn and an adjacent usually awnless male/sterile pedicelled spikelet. The sessile unit is roughly 5.5–10 mm including its pointed callus; the companion is often ~5–15 mm. Existing flowering panels show overlapping parts, not a fully traced measured pair.
tiles.short: Upper pair: fertile SESSILE + male/sterile PEDICELLED

tiles.heading: 04 · EXPOSE GLUMES AND SHARP CALLUS
tiles.details: Dissect a mature fertile sessile spikelet. Its firm dark lower glume is roughly spikelet-length with commonly 5–9 veins; the narrower upper glume is commonly 3-veined. The bearded copper-brown callus at the base is a distinct needle-sharp ~2–3 mm structure, not an awn. Do not label its tip or glume vein counts from a distant mature tangle.
tiles.status: NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO — DISSECTED GLUMES AND CALIBRATED CALLUS

tiles.heading: 05 · FOLLOW THE SINGLE FERTILE LEMMA AWN
tiles.details: A lower sterile lemma is thin and awnless; the upper fertile lemma is usually ~3–5 mm, one-veined, and produces ONE long bent and twisted awn. Published awn ranges vary (~50–80 mm in AusGrass, up to ~120 mm in Tropical Forages). Panels 7–9 reveal actual awns, anthers and stigmas, but do not prove a measured lemma insertion. Feathery stigmas and projecting anthers are NOT awns.
tiles.short: Upper fertile lemma ~3–5 mm; one bent/twisted awn ~5–12 cm
tiles.status: NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO — LEMMA ORIGIN AND FULL-LENGTH AWN RULER

tiles.heading: 06 · SEPARATE KR AND LITTLE BLUESTEM
tiles.details: Panel 10 is introduced KR bluestem, NOT tanglehead; compare the attachment of several radiating racemes and their shorter awns. Panel 11 is native little bluestem, NOT tanglehead; compare its separated silvery fuzzy branches with tanglehead's narrow dark awn spire. Silver bluestem and Kleberg bluestem also overlap in habit; use a true attached spikelet pair and collar, not brown color or a single fuzzy photo.
tiles.short: Tanglehead's long twisted awns ≠ KR's shorter multi-raceme heads
tiles.status: FIELD LOOK-ALIKE CUES; SAME-SCALE LOCAL COMPARISONS MISSING

steps.title: 1 · First, recognize the plant
steps.look_for: TANGLEHEAD: first identify the slim upright perennial tuft and solitary/narrow flowering raceme. Then verify the ACTUAL short MEMBRANOUS FRINGED LIGULE at the blade-sheath collar (new Harry Rose images), its initially green furry paired spikelet axis, actual hanging pollen anthers versus short feathery stigmas, and long dark twisted awns that form a tangled terminal spire at maturity. The lower raceme has similar male/sterile spikelet pairs; upper pairs become dissimilar (fertile sessile with long lemma awn plus sterile/male pedicelled neighbor). The very sharp bearded 2–3 mm basal callus MUST be measured on an actual dissected pair; image-level proof is not in current gallery. DO NOT use brown color or old grass tuft alone.
steps.why_it_matters: Start with the recorded recognition characters before making a species identification.

steps.title: 2 · Examine the whole plant
steps.look_for: BEGIN habit: panel 3 shows a dry erect tuft; it does not show a root crown. Then trace the flowering culm to its usually narrow spike-like raceme rather than assuming every similar grassy tuft is tanglehead.
steps.why_it_matters: Habit and growing context are supporting evidence, not proof of hidden roots or rhizomes.

steps.title: 3 · Inspect leaves, collar and nodes
steps.look_for: At the inner blade–sheath junction, lift the blade to expose the short pale membrane and its fringed margin. Panels 4–5 are authentic Harry Rose collar close-ups; longer adjacent sheath-mouth hairs are separate and must not be measured as the ligule. Published treatments differ in describing a hair fringe versus a ciliate membrane; keep the distinction visible.
steps.why_it_matters: Examine the real structures; the photo may not expose or measure all the described characters.

steps.title: 4 · Check the flowering structure
steps.look_for: Trace a single rachis joint under 10–20×. Basal pairs can be similar-looking and awnless; upper pairs differ: a fertile sessile unit with one long awn and an adjacent usually awnless male/sterile pedicelled spikelet. The sessile unit is roughly 5.5–10 mm including its pointed callus; the companion is often ~5–15 mm. Existing flowering panels show overlapping parts, not a fully traced measured pair.
steps.why_it_matters: Use an attached, correctly identified specimen when deciding the flower or spikelet structures.

steps.title: 5 · Compare similar grasses
steps.look_for: Unlike KR/silver bluestem (Bothriochloa spp.), tanglehead has strikingly long, dark twisting awns from sessile spikelets on narrow racemes; at maturity the awns can intertwine into a spire. Little bluestem (Schizachyrium scoparium) is recognizable by its fine silvery seed tufts and flowering-branch architecture rather than a concentrated dark tangle. Introduced Dichanthium can have rather fingerlike or branched racemes, with different paired spikelet/glume characters. Confirm under lens, not from posture alone. The sharp hairy callus and sessile + pedicelled companion structure are key unphotographed microcharacters.
steps.why_it_matters: Confirm at least two independent botanical characters; do not remove a native candidate from color alone.

intro: TANGLEHEAD: first identify the slim upright perennial tuft and solitary/narrow flowering raceme. Then verify the ACTUAL short MEMBRANOUS FRINGED LIGULE at the blade-sheath collar (new Harry Rose images), its initially green furry paired spikelet axis, actual hanging pollen anthers versus short feathery stigmas, and long dark twisted awns that form a tangled terminal spire at maturity. The lower raceme has similar male/sterile spikelet pairs; upper pairs become dissimilar (fertile sessile with long lemma awn plus sterile/male pedicelled neighbor). The very sharp bearded 2–3 mm basal callus MUST be measured on an actual dissected pair; image-level proof is not in current gallery. DO NOT use brown color or old grass tuft alone.
memory_rule: TRUE collar hair-fringed MEMBRANE → lower green similar sterile spikelet pairs → upper awned fertile sessile spikelet + unawned pedicelled partner (requires dissection) → LONG dark twisting awns eventually tangle. Dark red feathery STIGMAS and brown pollen ANTHERS are NOT awns.
safety_note: Ten source-labelled species JPEGs are recorded and physically present in the canonical images directory, including SIX Harry Rose CC BY 2.0 Australian collar/flowering images and the Bernard DUPONT CC BY-SA 2.0 South African mature-awn photograph. These are not Hays-vouchered specimens; the original coanne CC BY-NC image remains subject to noncommercial public-use conditions. The collar photographs show membrane/fringe but no ruler; overlapping spikelet views do not resolve the attached sessile/pedicelled pair, exact glumes, the 2–3 mm callus tip or complete measured awn. The two local look-alike comparison panels are OTHER species. Keep accurate creator/source/license attribution and do not infer microscopic arrows or declare the live Pages build verified.
field_rule: Walk up from erect tuft to narrow raceme; verify actual short membranous fringed ligule; then true reproductive pattern: basal similar paired spikelets and upper unlike paired members, awned sessile fertile plus unawned pedicellate neighbor; mature long dark contorted awns and pungent brown bearded callus. Fine pair/callus requires attached scaled specimen. Photos from Australia are illustrative, not Texas occurrences.
photo_data_caution: Missing or restricted comparison photographs have not been replaced by guesses. Source statements are not proof the associated structure is visible in any available photo.
